name: Endothelial FGF-2 / VEGF / VEGFR2 / PI3K-Akt-eNOS and angiogenesis
driver: unresolved; waveform/duty and duration implicated (same 2 mT/50 Hz sine is anti-angiogenic, pulsed 1.5-5 mT bursts pro-angiogenic)
driver_note: Peng 2020 is the only paired comparison (15 Hz/1.5 mT vs 30 Hz/3.0 mT, calc. dB/dt 0.14 vs 0.57 T/s) and B, f and dB/dt rose together. Delle Monache 2013: 2 mT, 50 Hz sinusoid reduced proliferation, tubulogenesis and VEGFR2. Prucha 2019: rectangular 340 us pulses at 72 Hz, 4 mT changed proliferation, the 5 kHz AM sine mode did not (abstract). Both FGF-2 and PI3K-Akt-eNOS arms are blocked by pathway inhibitors, so the mechanism is real in those systems; the activating physical quantity is not isolated.

dBdt_Ts.basis: computed; sine assumed where waveform not stated; Prucha assumes a 340 us rise (rise not reported)

windows.schedule: 45 min-8 h/day for 1-4 weeks in vivo; 4-24 h continuous in cells; VEGF release 3.2x at 24 h (Vincenzi 2020)

evidence: mouse/rat in vivo plus HUVEC; two or three lineages; Li 2015 and Hao 2014 share a group and a protocol
caveat: Goto 2010: VEGF, Tie-2, Ang-1 unchanged in marrow, FGF-2 and Ang-2 up. PEMF alone did not rescue HUVEC apoptosis (Cheng 2017). Pro-angiogenic gene induction in RPE (Oladnabi) is a safety flag. Sheikh 2012 is direct E-field at 7.5 GHz vs 60 Hz, not magnetic.

name: HIF-1a / hypoxia axis
driver_note: HIF-1a up with VEGF in Peng 2020 and Hao 2014. In astrocytes (1.5 mT, 75 Hz, 1.3 ms, 24 h) VEGF release rose 3.2x but was HIF-1a independent (chetomin no effect, HIF-1a protein unchanged).

name: Microvascular blood flow, vasodilation and oxygenation
driver: unresolved; the one mechanistically controlled study is E-field / NO driven with B undefined; healthy-skin flow shows no B dose-response
driver_note: Bragin 2014 (rat cortex, 27.12 MHz, 3 ms bursts at 5 Hz, tissue E about 6 V/m, SAR 40 mW/kg): arterioles 26.4 to 29.1 um (p<0.01), capillary RBC velocity +5.5 %, NADH to 94.7 %, L-NAME abolished everything. The effect was not significant by 3 h. Schuhfried 2005 found no skin-flow change at 100 uT/30 Hz or 8.4 mT/10 Hz (28-fold dB/dt spread, calc. 0.019 vs 0.53 T/s). Static fields reduce capillary RBC velocity only above ~500 mT (Brix 2008, 587 mT gave -40 %), with dB/dt = 0.
caveat: Sun 2016: vein velocity rose but diameter and laser-Doppler flux did not. Biermann 2020: both legs rose equally (time/rest artefact). Mayrovitz 2025 (n=6, 7.8 Hz rotating magnets) lowered perfusion. Effects appear more reliably in impaired tissue than healthy skin.

name: Fibroblast / keratinocyte proliferation, collagen and wound closure
driver: current density (inverted U, Cleary 1988) and duration; no controlled B vs dB/dt test
driver_note: Cleary 1988 (applied current, 1 ms unipolar pulses at 1 Hz): J time-averaged 7 mA/m2 gave +32 % proliferation, 3.5 mA/m2 also effective, 1.8 mA/m2 no effect, >10 mA/m2 inhibitory, effect only with explants parallel to the field. It is applied current, not induced, but it is the one quantitative window. Direct-E-field work (Korraah 1-10 V/m; Wolf-Goldberg 1000 V/m) is far above induced PEMF E (~0.01 V/m at r = 1 cm for the IGEA signal) and cannot be used as a PEMF threshold. Continuous 24 h at 7 mT/50 Hz raised cytokines while 1 h/day did not (via review).

windows.animal_wound: Callaghan: closure 11 vs 15 d (WT), 16 vs 24 d (diabetic), via review; Cheing: closure benefit at d10 and d14, none later, endpoint closure ~99 % in both

evidence: in vitro, STZ and db/db models; Cochrane venous (3 RCTs, 94) and pressure (2 RCTs, 60) ulcer reviews unclear/no robust benefit
caveat: Cleary's original note called the inverted U "4-fold wide"; that gloss is not supported and is dropped. Czyz 2011 post-blepharoplasty RCT null on oedema.

name: Skeletal muscle (myoblast differentiation, satellite cells, recovery)
driver: timing / duty (Terrie) and TRPC1 route; a static-B route also exists at uT; dB/dt not tested
driver_note: Terrie 2022 (2 mT, 75 Hz, 1.3 ms; induced probe voltage 5 mV): in 2D 22 h/day beat 2 h/day on myotube area; in 3D 2 h/day beat 22 h/day, and starting on day 8 (after fusion) gave fusion index 66 % vs 51 % (day 1) vs 28 % (static). Static 60-400 uT accelerated myotube formation via ryanodine-receptor Ca release (Surma 2014) and shielding to 0.3 uT inhibited growth, so B acts with dB/dt = 0. Mueller 2017 static-field null.

windows.schedule: 10 min single dose (Yap); 2 h/day vs 22 h/day, 4-16 d, start day 1 vs 8 (Terrie)

evidence: in vitro (one or two labs); DOMS RCT (n=30, parameters not reported) improved soreness but not peak torque
confidence: in vitro low-moderate; in vivo low
caveat: rPMS strength gains (Ogawa 2019) are a high-dB/dt neural mechanism and must not be pooled with low-dB/dt PEMF. No CK-based PEMF study was retrieved.

name: Lymphatic / oedema, tissue oxygenation, iron axis
driver_note: Nothing retrieved on lymphatic function. Post-blepharoplasty RF patch null on oedema. NADH autofluorescence -5.3 % lasting ~3 h (Bragin). 15 Hz/3.82 mT, 40 min/day for 2 months changed neither ferritin, hepcidin nor tissue iron (Yang 2025, calc. 0.36 T/s).

name: NO / eNOS node (common to vascular targets)
driver_note: Lowest B with an eNOS result: 0.6 mT, 50 Hz in osteoblasts, eNOS phosphorylated inside cilia, abolished by L-NAME (He 2022). In vivo vasodilation NO-dependent at ~6 V/m RF. Serum NO unchanged in hypertensives, a poor readout.
confidence: moderate that NO mediates; low that any particular field quantity activates it

name: Regime split in musculoskeletal PEMF (low-B vs high-dB/dt EMTT)
driver_note: Leyva Martinez 2026 (28 studies, 1060 patients, SWiM): high-dB/dt EMTT (>60 kT/s) effective in structural disease; <5 mT often indistinguishable from placebo; one 80 mT/3 Hz trial null in myofascial pain; waveform and dB/dt rarely reported. The authors call it exploratory.
